# NavSentinel North-Star — External Research Report

**Question (5 angles):** on-device ML in MV3 · FP-elimination & warning science · competitive landscape · MV3 escape hatches & visual brand-impersonation · local feedback capture.

## Executive summary

A local-first MV3 near-zero-FP companion is feasible. On-device Gemini Nano via the Prompt API gives zero-network scam classification in extensions (Chrome 138+); near-zero FP is achievable (AV-C 2025: 95 percent block, ~zero FA) but alerts must be minimized per warning science; Tranco (filtered) is the benign prior and conformal rejection controls FP under drift; Chrome built-in lags and misses interaction-level attacks; the Side Panel API is the non-interruptive advisor surface. See findings for per-angle detail.</parameter>

## Confirmed findings (4)

### Angle 1: Chrome's Prompt API enables a fully on-device, zero-network scam classifier in an MV3 extension with JSON-Schema output and full param tuning; Chrome already ships local Gemini Nano scam detection. Merged 3-0, claims 0-5.
- **Confidence:** high
- **Sources:** https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/prompt-api · https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/structured-output-for-prompt-api · https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/safety-security/how-were-using-ai-to-combat-the-latest-scams/
- **Evidence:** Prompt API docs: no data sent to Google; no network after initial download. JSON Schema via responseConstraint (Chrome 137); topK/temperature exclusive to the Extensions path (stable Chrome 138). Google blog: on-device Gemini Nano adds a scam-defense layer for Enhanced Protection, deployed against tech-support scams. Caveat: Enhanced Protection still sends local LLM signals to Safe Browsing for the verdict; a first-party extension classifier keeps I/O in-context with zero per-call network calls.

### Angle 2a: Near-zero FP and high phishing-block coexist; the dominant FP cost is warning habituation, so minimize alerts and tune for the ~0 percent ideal click-through of true-positive warnings. Merged 3-0/2-1, claims 6,7,8,9,10,19.
- **Confidence:** high
- **Sources:** https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity13/technical-sessions/presentation/akhawe · https://www.usenix.org/system/files/conference/soups2016/soups2016-paper-porter-felt.pdf · https://www.av-comparatives.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/phishing_comp_Q4-2025.pdf
- **Evidence:** Akhawe/Felt 2013 (25.4M impressions): click-through varies by UX (Chrome SSL 70.2 vs Firefox 33.0 percent); Safe Browsing FP negligible so ideal malware/phishing click-through ~0 percent. Porter Felt 2016 (n=1329): tech-savvy users misread indicators; HTTPS no longer an anti-phishing signal. AV-C 2025: Q4 every product 0 FA on 250 clean URLs; only Malwarebytes and Webroot logged one FA each all year; Avast/Norton 95 percent block. Caveat: clean set small/banking-skewed.

### Angle 2b: Raw top-site lists are unsafe as an allowlist; Tranco is hardened and usable if filtered. Conformal evaluation with rejection (Transcendent) uses per-class credibility p-value thresholds via constrained F1 optimization under bounded rejection, beating raw probabilities. Merged 3-0/2-1, claims 11-16.
- **Confidence:** high
- **Sources:** https://tranco-list.eu/assets/tranco-ndss19.pdf · https://s2lab.cs.ucl.ac.uk/downloads/transcending.pdf
- **Evidence:** Tranco NDSS 2019: one HTTP request enters Alexa's top million; rank 28798 achievable; 4 phishing sites in Alexa top 10000; Quad9 whitelisted all Majestic domains; Majestic held 2162 malicious domains; Tranco varies 0.6 percent daily, needs 4x manipulation effort; caveat: not manipulation-proof, still has adult/gambling/streaming domains, so filter. Transcend (IEEE EuroS+P 2022): low credibility = probability i.i.d. violated (OOD/drift); calibration maximizes F1 of kept elements under 15 percent rejection (~20 vs 80/day labeling capacity); credibility alone beats raw probabilities (kept-F1 .829/.762/.950 vs .531/.388/.532), which grow volatile under drift. Fits single-user active learning.

### Angles 3+4: Chrome built-in protection lags third-party products (URL-blocklist coverage only, not interaction-level attacks); the Side Panel API (Chrome 114+) is a persistent, non-interruptive advisor UI needing no host permissions. Merged 2-1/3-0, claims 17,18,20,21.
- **Confidence:** high
- **Sources:** https://www.av-comparatives.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/phishing_comp_Q4-2025.pdf · https://developer.chrome.com/blog/extension-side-panel-launch
- **Evidence:** AV-C Nov 2025: Chrome+SafeBrowsing blocked only 41 percent of 250 phishing URLs in Q4 (lowest of six browsers: Edge 65, Firefox/Opera 74, Avast/Norton Secure 85), 0 FA; full-year Chrome 56, Edge 69, Avast/Norton 95 percent. Measures URL/blocklist coverage, NOT interaction-level attacks (clickjacking, DoubleClickjacking, ClickFix, clipboard-hijack), the differentiating gap; per-vendor FP for Netcraft/TrafficLight/Guardio/Malwarebytes Browser Guard/uBlock not quantified. Chrome dev blog: Side Panel API from Chrome 114, persistent UI alongside the page; showing UI without host permissions is a privacy win reducing install warnings; needs only the sidePanel permission. Caveat: reading page DOM from the panel still needs content scripts/host permissions (w3c webextensions issue 387).

## Caveats & what was refuted

Chrome built-in AI moves fast; re-verify model availability/disk(2.7-4GB)/WebGPU gating. Enhanced Protection still makes a Safe Browsing network call for the verdict (local layer, not end-to-end zero-network). REFUTED (do not carry forward): on-device LLM detecting zero-day scams (1-2); MV3 DNR ceilings and storage limits blocking large/bloom-filter blocklists (0-3 each) — these WEAKEN any MV3 blocklist constraint. AV-C FP is a small banking-skewed 250-URL set, not internet-scale. NOT covered by surviving claims: TF.js/ONNX/WebGPU in MV3 offscreen docs; visual brand-impersonation SOTA (Phishpedia/PhishIntention/VisualPhishNet/PhishLLM, hashing vs Siamese embeddings); native-messaging + Firefox blocking webRequest; rrweb/feature-vector snapshots; per-vendor competitor FP rates.

## Refuted claims (transparency)

- "The on-device LLM approach provides instant analysis of risky websites and can detect previously-unseen (zero-day) scams without prior exposure to that scam type." (vote 1-2, https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/safety-security/how-were-using-ai-to-combat-the-latest-scams/)
- "MV3's declarativeNetRequest imposes hard rule-count ceilings (30,000 guaranteed minimum static rules, ~350,000 global limit in Chrome Canary, and a maximum of 5,000 dynamic and session rules), which a security extension cannot use to represent blocklists containing millions of malicious/phishing domains." (vote 0-3, https://github.com/w3c/webextensions/issues/82)
- "MV3 makes the bloom-filter data structure that MV2 malware/phishing extensions relied on to hold huge blocklists infeasible, because storage.local is too small/slow for millions of keys and storage.session is capped at 1MB." (vote 0-3, https://github.com/w3c/webextensions/issues/82)
